question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Showing sadness and tears, or tending to cry easily.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Lachrymose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Lachrymose" means tearful, given to weeping, from Latin lacrima meaning tear. (रोने वाला)
◦ Example: Her lachrymose speech at the farewell moved everyone to tears.

 

• The root "lacrima" (Latin for tear) also appears in lachrymal (relating to tears or tear glands).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Morose (उदास और चिड़चिड़ा): Sullen, ill-tempered and gloomy.

 

• Option 3: Lugubrious (शोकाकुल): Looking or sounding sad and dismal.

 

• Option 4: Petulant (बचकाने ढंग से चिड़चिड़ा): Childishly sulky or easily irritated.

 

NOTE

 

• Other mood-related SSC words: Morose (sullen and gloomy), Lugubrious (mournful), Petulant (childishly irritable), Sanguine (cheerfully optimistic), Phlegmatic (calm and unemotional).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों का समान रूप से उपयोग करने वाला): Able to use both hands equally well

2. Bibliophile (पुस्तक-प्रेमी): A person who loves books

3. Cacophony (कर्कश ध्वनि): A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds

4. Diffident (संकोची): Lacking self-confidence; shy

5. Ephemeral (क्षणभंगुर): Lasting for a very short time

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Conformity to facts; truthfulness or accuracy of what is said.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Veracity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Veracity" means truthfulness or accuracy, from Latin verus meaning true. (सत्यता)
◦ Example: The journalist questioned the veracity of the minister's claims.

 

• Do not confuse Veracity (truthfulness) with the similar-sounding Voracity (greed for food) or Audacity (boldness).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Audacity (दुस्साहस): Boldness or daring, often shockingly so.

 

• Option 2: Voracity (पेटूपन, अतृप्त भूख): Extreme eagerness or greed, especially for food.

 

• Option 4: Mendacity (असत्यता): The quality of being untruthful.

 

NOTE

 

• Words built on Latin verus (true): Verify (to confirm as true), Verdict (a judgment), Aver (to assert as true), Verisimilitude (appearance of being true).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Frugal (मितव्ययी): Sparing or economical with resources

2. Gullible (भोला-भाला): Easily deceived or tricked

3. Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes pleasure is the most important thing in life

4. Immaculate (निष्कलंक): Perfectly clean or tidy; without flaw

5. Jubilant (अति प्रसन्न): Feeling or expressing great happiness

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who makes an excessive show of knowledge, especially about trivial or minor details.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pedant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pedant" means one who shows off knowledge, from French pedant, ultimately from Italian pedante. (आडंबरपूर्ण विद्वान)
◦ Example: The professor was such a pedant that he corrected every minor grammatical error.

 

• A Pedant is obsessed with rules and minor details, unlike a Dilettante, who only dabbles superficially.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Dilettante (शौकिया कलाप्रेमी): A person with a superficial interest in an art or subject.

 

• Option 2: Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of taste.

 

• Option 3: Charlatan (पाखंडी, धोखेबाज़): A person falsely claiming expertise or skill.

 

NOTE

 

• Related SSC words for types of people: Dilettante (superficial dabbler), Charlatan (fraudulent expert), Connoisseur (genuine expert or judge), Polymath (person with knowledge of many subjects), Erudite (deeply learned person).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Kleptomaniac (चोरी करने की मानसिक बीमारी वाला व्यक्ति): A person with an uncontrollable urge to steal

2. Laconic (अल्पभाषी): Using very few words

3. Misanthrope (मानव-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes humankind

4. Nomad (घुमंतू): A person with no fixed home, who moves from place to place

5. Omnipotent (सर्वशक्तिमान): Having unlimited power

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Anagram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anagram" means word formed by rearranging letters, from Greek ana- (back, again) and gramma (letter). (शब्द-विन्यास)
◦ Example: Listen is an anagram of silent.

 

• Do not confuse Anagram (rearranged letters) with Acronym (formed from initial letters) or Palindrome (reads the same both ways).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Acronym (आद्याक्षर शब्द): A word formed from the initial letters of other words.

 

• Option 3: Palindrome (व्यत्क्रमानुलोमी शब्द): A word that reads the same backward as forward.

 

• Option 4: Synonym (पर्यायवाची शब्द): A word having the same meaning as another.

 

NOTE

 

• Word-formation family: Acronym (e.g. LASER), Palindrome (e.g. madam), Homonym (same spelling or sound, different meaning), Synonym (same meaning), Antonym (opposite meaning).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philanthropist (परोपकारी, दानवीर): A person who helps others, especially through charitable donations

2. Quandary (दुविधा): A state of uncertainty over what to do

3. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in seclusion, avoiding others

4. Sceptic (संशयवादी): A person who doubts accepted beliefs

5. Taciturn (कम बोलने वाला): Reserved or uncommunicative in speech

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Having or showing great knowledge, especially through education and reading.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Erudite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Erudite" means deeply learned or scholarly, from Latin eruditus, past participle of erudire (to instruct, free from rudeness). (विद्वान)
◦ Example: The erudite scholar delivered a lecture full of references to ancient texts.

 

• Erudite relates to formal, book-based learning, while Sagacious relates more to practical wisdom and judgment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Sagacious (बुद्धिमान, दूरदर्शी): Having or showing keen judgment and wisdom.

 

• Option 3: Loquacious (बातूनी): Very talkative.

 

• Option 4: Illiterate (निरक्षर): Unable to read or write; lacking education.

 

NOTE

 

• Words describing knowledge or intellect: Sagacious (wise), Astute (shrewd), Sapient (wise, discerning), Scholarly (learned); opposite: Illiterate (uneducated).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ubiquitous (सर्वव्यापी): Present or found everywhere

2. Vindictive (प्रतिशोधी): Having a strong desire for revenge

3. Wanderlust (घुमक्कड़ी की प्रबल इच्छा): A strong desire to travel

4. Xenophobia (विदेशियों के प्रति भय या घृणा): Fear or hatred of foreigners

5. Zealot (कट्टरपंथी): A person who is fanatically committed to a cause

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is highly skilled or has extensive knowledge in a particular field.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Expert.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Expert" means a highly skilled specialist, from Latin expertus, past participle of experiri (to try, test). (विशेषज्ञ)
◦ Example: A financial expert was called in to review the company's accounts.

 

• Expert is the opposite of Novice (beginner) and Layman (a non-specialist).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to and inexperienced in a field.

 

• Option 3: Amateur (शौकिया व्यक्ति): A person who engages in an activity for pleasure, not as a profession.

 

• Option 4: Layman (सामान्य व्यक्ति): A person without specialized or professional knowledge.

 

NOTE

 

• Level-of-skill family: Novice (beginner), Amateur (non-professional), Veteran (long-experienced person), Virtuoso (exceptionally skilled, especially in the arts), Layman (ordinary non-expert).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Altruist (परोपकारी, परार्थी): A person unselfishly concerned for others' welfare

2. Belligerent (लड़ाकू, आक्रामक): Hostile and aggressive

3. Clairvoyant (दिव्यदृष्टि रखने वाला): A person who claims to perceive future or hidden events

4. Docile (आज्ञाकारी): Ready to accept control; easily managed

5. Egoist (स्वार्थी, अहंकारी): A person who is excessively self-centred

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A short explanatory note or comment added to a text or diagram.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Annotation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Annotation" means an explanatory note, from Latin annotare (to mark, note). (टिप्पणी)
◦ Example: The editor added an annotation to clarify the archaic word used in the poem.

 

• An Annotation can appear anywhere in a text, while a Footnote specifically appears at the bottom of the page.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Footnote (पाद-टिप्पणी): A note printed at the bottom of a page referring to the text above.

 

• Option 3: Preface (प्रस्तावना): An introduction to a book explaining its purpose.

 

• Option 4: Appendix (परिशिष्ट): Supplementary material placed at the end of a book.

 

NOTE

 

• Book-structure family: Preface (introduction), Appendix (supplementary end-matter), Footnote (bottom-of-page note), Glossary (list of difficult word meanings), Index (alphabetical list of topics with page numbers).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Fastidious (चूज़ी, नुक्ताचीनी करने वाला): Very attentive to detail; hard to please

2. Garrulous (बकबक करने वाला): Excessively talkative

3. Hermit (सन्यासी, वैरागी): A person living in solitude, especially for religious reasons

4. Iconoclast (परंपरा भंजक): A person who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions

5. Jingoist (उग्र राष्ट्रवादी): A person having extreme, aggressive nationalism

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The sound of a bell rung slowly, especially to announce a death or funeral.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Knell.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Knell" means sound of a funeral bell, from Old English cnyll, imitative of the bell's sound. (मृत्यु घंटानाद)
◦ Example: The knell of the church bell announced the old king's death.

 

• Knell specifically signals death or doom (as in 'death knell'), unlike Chime or Peal, which can also describe joyful sounds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Chime (घंटियों की सुरीली ध्वनि): A melodious sound made by a set of bells.

 

• Option 3: Peal (घंटों की तेज़ गूँजती ध्वनि): A loud ringing of bells, or a sudden burst of sound.

 

• Option 4: Toll (धीरे-धीरे घंटा बजाना): To ring a bell slowly and repeatedly.

 

NOTE

 

• Bell-sound family: Toll (to ring slowly), Peal (loud ringing), Chime (melodious ringing), Clang (loud metallic sound), Knell (funeral bell, symbolic of doom).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Knack (विशेष कुशलता): A special skill or talent

2. Linguist (भाषाविद्): A person skilled in foreign languages or the study of languages

3. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारों वाला व्यक्ति): An unorthodox or independent-minded person

4. Nostalgic (भूतकाल की याद में डूबा): Feeling a sentimental longing for the past

5. Optimist (आशावादी): A person who tends to expect the best outcome

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The mental state of being fully aware and focused on the present moment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mindfulness.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Mindfulness" means awareness of the present moment, a term popularized in psychology and meditation practice for present-moment awareness. (जागरूकता)
◦ Example: Practicing mindfulness for ten minutes a day can reduce stress.

 

• Mindfulness is the opposite of Reverie (daydreaming) or Complacency (unaware self-satisfaction) — it means being consciously present.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Nostalgia (अतीत की याद, गृह-विरह): A sentimental longing for the past.

 

• Option 2: Reverie (दिवास्वप्न): A state of being pleasantly lost in one's thoughts; daydream.

 

• Option 3: Complacency (आत्मसंतोष): Uncritical self-satisfaction, often unaware of danger.

 

NOTE

 

• Mental-state family: Reverie (daydream), Nostalgia (longing for the past), Complacency (self-satisfied unawareness), Equanimity (calmness under pressure), Introspection (examining one's own thoughts).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Pessimist (निराशावादी): A person who expects the worst outcome

2. Quack (झोलाछाप डॉक्टर): A person who dishonestly claims to have medical skill

3. Recalcitrant (अवज्ञाकारी, हठी): Having an obstinately uncooperative attitude

4. Somnambulist (नींद में चलने वाला व्यक्ति): A person who walks in their sleep

5. Truant (बिना अनुमति स्कूल से गायब रहने वाला छात्र): A student who stays away from school without permission

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Just beginning to appear or develop.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Incipient.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Incipient" means just beginning to exist or appear, from Latin incipere (to begin). (प्रारंभिक)
◦ Example: Doctors detected an incipient infection before it could spread.

 

• Do not confuse Incipient (just starting) with Imminent (about to happen soon) — incipient refers to an early stage, imminent to timing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Imminent (आसन्न, निकट भविष्य में होने वाला): About to happen very soon.

 

• Option 3: Obsolete (अप्रचलित): No longer in use; outdated.

 

• Option 4: Decrepit (जर्जर): Worn out or weakened by age or hard use.

 

NOTE

 

• Stage-of-development family: Nascent (just coming into existence), Embryonic (in a very early stage), Incipient (just beginning), Obsolete (outdated, no longer used), Decrepit (worn out by age).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Usurper (सत्ता हड़पने वाला): A person who takes a position of power illegally

2. Vagrant (आवारा, बेघर व्यक्ति): A person without a settled home or regular work

3. Workaholic (काम का आदी व्यक्ति): A person who works excessively

4. Yokel (गंवार, देहाती व्यक्ति): An unsophisticated person from the countryside

5. Zenith (चरमोत्कर्ष, शिखर): The highest point or peak

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The height of an object or point in relation to sea level.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Altitude.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Altitude" means height above sea level, from Latin altitudo, from altus (high). (ऊँचाई)
◦ Example: The plane was flying at an altitude of 35,000 feet.

 

• Do not confuse Altitude (height) with the similar-sounding Latitude (a geographic north-south position).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Latitude (अक्षांश): Angular distance of a place north or south of the equator.

 

• Option 3: Longitude (देशांतर): Angular distance of a place east or west of a standard meridian.

 

• Option 4: Depth (गहराई): The distance from the top or surface downward.

 

NOTE

 

• Geography and measurement family: Latitude (north-south position), Longitude (east-west position), Depth (downward distance), Elevation (height of land above sea level, a close synonym of altitude).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ambivalent (दुविधाग्रस्त): Having mixed feelings about something

2. Benevolent (दयालु, परोपकारी): Well meaning and kindly

3. Congenital (जन्मजात): Existing from birth

4. Deference (सम्मानपूर्वक समर्पण): Humble submission and respect

5. Effervescent (उत्साह से भरपूर): Vivacious and enthusiastic

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Excessively eager to please or obey someone, often in a servile manner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Obsequious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Obsequious" means excessively eager to please, servile, from Latin obsequi (to comply with). (चापलूस)
◦ Example: The obsequious waiter kept complimenting every customer to earn a bigger tip.

 

• Obsequious behaviour is a negative trait — it describes a flatterer or 'yes-man', not simply someone polite or helpful.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Arrogant (अहंकारी): Having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance.

 

• Option 2: Indifferent (उदासीन): Having no particular interest or concern.

 

• Option 3: Belligerent (आक्रामक, युद्धप्रिय): Hostile and aggressive.

 

NOTE

 

• Flattery and servility family: Sycophant (a flatterer, noun), Servile (excessively submissive), Fawning (displaying exaggerated flattery), Toady (a servile flatterer).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Fallacy (भ्रांति, तर्कदोष): A mistaken belief based on unsound argument

2. Gregarious (मिलनसार): Fond of company; sociable

3. Haphazard (अव्यवस्थित, यादृच्छिक): Lacking any organization; random

4. Impeccable (निर्दोष, त्रुटिहीन): Without fault; flawless

5. Juvenile (किशोर, बचकाना): Relating to young people; childish

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who has escaped from custody or is fleeing to avoid arrest or punishment under the law.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fugitive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Fugitive" means one fleeing from the law, from Latin fugere (to flee). (भगोड़ा)
◦ Example: The fugitive was captured at the border after a week-long manhunt.

 

• Do not confuse Fugitive (fleeing arrest or punishment) with Deserter (specifically abandoning military duty).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Vagabond (आवारा, घुमक्कड़): A person who wanders from place to place without a home.

 

• Option 2: Deserter (भगोड़ा सैनिक): A soldier who abandons military duty without permission.

 

• Option 4: Trespasser (अतिक्रमणकारी): A person who enters someone's property unlawfully.

 

NOTE

 

• Words for people evading authority: Deserter (military), Absconder (one who flees to avoid legal consequences), Runaway (one who has fled home or custody), Outlaw (a criminal beyond the law's protection).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Kudos (प्रशंसा, श्रेय): Praise for an achievement

2. Lethargic (सुस्त, आलसी): Sluggish and lacking energy

3. Munificent (अत्यंत उदार, दानशील): Very generous

4. Nefarious (अत्यंत दुष्ट, पापपूर्ण): Wicked or criminal

5. Obstinate (हठी, जिद्दी): Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Easily annoyed or irritated; bad-tempered.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Grumpy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Grumpy" means easily annoyed or irritable, related to the word grumble, suggesting a complaining, irritable mood. (चिड़चिड़ा)
◦ Example: He gets grumpy if he doesn't have his morning coffee.

 

• Grumpy is the opposite of Amiable or Genial — both describe a pleasant, friendly temperament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Amiable (मिलनसार): Having a friendly and pleasant manner.

 

• Option 2: Docile (आज्ञाकारी, सीधा): Ready to accept control; easily managed.

 

• Option 3: Genial (सौम्य, मिलनसार): Friendly and cheerful in manner.

 

NOTE

 

• Temperament family: Irascible (easily angered), Petulant (childishly sulky), Amiable (friendly), Genial (warm and cheerful), Docile (calm and easily managed).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Prodigal (फ़िज़ूलख़र्ची करने वाला): Wastefully extravagant

2. Querulous (शिकायती): Complaining in a whining manner

3. Ravenous (अत्यंत भूखा): Extremely hungry

4. Stoic (दुख-सुख में अविचलित रहने वाला): A person who endures hardship without complaint

5. Trivial (तुच्छ): Of little value or importance

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Naturally accompanying or occurring together with something else.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Concomitant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Concomitant" means occurring together with something else, from Latin concomitari (to accompany). (साथ-साथ)
◦ Example: Poverty is often a concomitant of unemployment.

 

• Concomitant implies one thing naturally accompanies another as a related effect, unlike Simultaneous, which only means happening at the same time without implying a causal link.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Simultaneous (समकालिक, एक साथ होने वाला): Occurring or done at exactly the same time.

 

• Option 3: Antecedent (पूर्ववर्ती): A thing that existed before or logically precedes another.

 

• Option 4: Subsequent (परवर्ती, बाद का): Coming after something in time; following.

 

NOTE

 

• Time-relation family: Antecedent (before), Subsequent (after), Simultaneous (at the same time), Concurrent (existing or happening at the same time), Concomitant (accompanying, naturally linked).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Unanimous (सर्वसम्मत): Fully in agreement

2. Volatile (अस्थिर, चंचल): Liable to change rapidly and unpredictably

3. Whimsical (सनकी, तरंगी): Playfully quaint or fanciful

4. Xenial (अतिथि-सत्कार से संबंधित): Relating to hospitality between host and guest

5. Yearning (तीव्र लालसा): An intense feeling of longing

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An imagined place or society in which everything is perfect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Utopia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Utopia" means a perfect imaginary society, coined by Thomas More from Greek ou (not) and topos (place), literally 'no place'. (आदर्श समाज)
◦ Example: The novel describes a utopia where poverty and crime do not exist.

 

• Utopia (ideal society) is the direct opposite of Dystopia (a nightmarish, oppressive society) — a very common SSC pairing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Dystopia (दुःस्वप्निल समाज): An imagined society characterized by great suffering or injustice.

 

• Option 3: Anarchy (अराजकता): Absence of government or law and order.

 

• Option 4: Oligarchy (अल्पतंत्र): Government by a small group of people.

 

NOTE

 

• Society and governance family: Dystopia (nightmarish imagined society), Anarchy (no government), Oligarchy (rule by a few), Autocracy (rule by one person with absolute power), Theocracy (rule by religious authority).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Amnesia (स्मृतिलोप): Loss of memory

2. Bourgeois (मध्यवर्गीय): Belonging to the middle class, especially materialistic

3. Cliché (घिसी-पिटी उक्ति): An overused phrase or idea

4. Debacle (पूर्ण विफलता, करारी हार): A sudden, ignominious failure

5. Enigma (रहस्यमय व्यक्ति या वस्तु): A person or thing that is mysterious and difficult to understand

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A place where animals are slaughtered for their meat.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Abattoir.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Abattoir" means a slaughterhouse for animals, from French abattre (to strike down, fell). (कसाईखाना)
◦ Example: The abattoir near the town processes hundreds of cattle every day.

 

• Do not confuse Abattoir (slaughterhouse) with Aviary (bird enclosure) or Apiary (bee-keeping place) — similar sounding but very different places.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Sanctuary (अभयारण्य): A place of refuge or protection, especially for wildlife.

 

• Option 3: Aviary (पक्षीशाला): A large enclosure for keeping birds.

 

• Option 4: Apiary (मधुमक्खी पालन स्थल): A place where bees are kept for honey production.

 

NOTE

 

• Animal-related place family: Aviary (birds), Apiary (bees), Sanctuary (protected wildlife area), Menagerie (a collection of wild animals kept for exhibition), Vivarium (enclosure for keeping live animals).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Facade (बनावटी रूप, बाहरी आवरण): A deceptive outward appearance

2. Gaffe (शर्मनाक भूल): An unintentional social blunder

3. Hindrance (बाधा, रुकावट): An obstacle that delays progress

4. Inertia (जड़ता): A tendency to remain unchanged

5. Jocular (हंसी-मजाक करने वाला): Fond of joking; humorous

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A doctor who specializes in the treatment of bones and the skeletal system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Orthopaedist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Orthopaedist" means a bone specialist doctor, from Greek orthos (straight, correct) and paidion (child), originally referring to correcting deformities in children. (हड्डी विशेषज्ञ)
◦ Example: After the fracture, she was referred to an orthopaedist for treatment.

 

• Medical specialist words usually end in "-ist" or "-ician"; the first part of the word tells you the body part or field treated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Cardiologist (हृदय रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in diseases of the heart.

 

• Option 2: Dermatologist (त्वचा रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in diseases of the skin.

 

• Option 3: Neurologist (तंत्रिका रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in disorders of the nervous system.

 

NOTE

 

• Medical specialist family: Cardiologist (heart), Dermatologist (skin), Neurologist (nervous system), Ophthalmologist (eyes), Pediatrician (children).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Kinship (रिश्तेदारी, नातेदारी): A sharing of characteristics or origins; family relationship

2. Legacy (विरासत, धरोहर): Something handed down from a predecessor

3. Meticulous (बहुत सावधान): Very careful and precise

4. Novice (नौसिखिया): A beginner in a field

5. Onlooker (तमाशबीन, दर्शक): A person who watches an event without taking part

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The state of abstaining from marriage, and often from sexual relations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Celibacy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Celibacy" means state of remaining unmarried, from Latin caelibatus, from caelebs (unmarried). (अविवाहित जीवन)
◦ Example: The monk took a vow of celibacy upon joining the monastery.

 

• Celibacy refers to staying unmarried (often by choice or vow), unlike Bigamy or Polygamy, which involve multiple marriages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Bigamy (द्विविवाह): The act of marrying someone while already married to another.

 

• Option 3: Monogamy (एकविवाह): The practice of having only one spouse at a time.

 

• Option 4: Polygamy (बहुविवाह): The practice of having more than one spouse at the same time.

 

NOTE

 

• Marriage-related family: Monogamy (one spouse), Bigamy (two spouses, illegal), Polygamy (multiple spouses), Polyandry (one wife, multiple husbands), Polygyny (one husband, multiple wives).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Panacea (सर्वरोगनाशक औषधि): A solution or remedy for all problems

2. Quagmire (दलदल, कठिन उलझन भरी स्थिति): A difficult, complex situation

3. Renegade (धर्मत्यागी, विद्रोही): A person who deserts a group or cause

4. Solitude (एकांत): The state of being alone

5. Tirade (लंबा गुस्सैल भाषण): A long angry speech of criticism

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A military or political group that rules a country, especially after seizing power by force.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Junta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Junta" means military rule of a government, from Spanish and Portuguese junta meaning 'council' or 'committee'. (सैन्य शासन)
◦ Example: The military junta seized control after overthrowing the elected president.

 

• A Junta usually comes to power through a Coup (the act of forcibly overthrowing a government) and then rules as a Regime.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Coup (तख्तापलट): A sudden, illegal seizure of power from a government.

 

• Option 3: Regime (शासन-प्रणाली): A government, especially an authoritarian one.

 

• Option 4: Cabinet (मंत्रिमंडल): A group of senior ministers responsible for government policy.

 

NOTE

 

• Governance and power-seizure family: Coup (sudden illegal seizure of power), Regime (a system of government), Insurgency (a rebellion against authority), Autocracy (rule by one person with absolute power).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Unscrupulous (बेईमान, अनैतिक): Having no moral principles

2. Vex (तंग करना, खिजाना): To make someone annoyed or worried

3. Wary (सतर्क, सावधान): Feeling cautious about danger

4. Yield (उपज देना, समर्पण करना): To produce, or to give way under pressure

5. Zest (उत्साह, जोश): Great enthusiasm and energy

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An account of a person's life written by someone other than that person.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Biography.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Biography" means life story written by another person, from Greek bios (life) and graphein (to write). (जीवनी)
◦ Example: She wrote a detailed biography of the freedom fighter after years of research.

 

• Remember: Biography = life story written by someone else; Autobiography = life story written by oneself, since the prefix "auto-" means self.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Autobiography (आत्मकथा): The story of a person's life written by that person themselves.

 

• Option 2: Memoir (संस्मरण): A written account of personal experiences or memorable events.

 

• Option 3: Obituary (मृत्युलेख): A published notice of a person's death, usually with a short account of their life.

 

NOTE

 

• Life-writing family: Autobiography (self-written life story), Memoir (personal recollections), Obituary (death notice), Eulogy (speech praising someone, often after death).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Cacophony (कर्कश ध्वनि): A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds

2. Frugal (मितव्ययी): Sparing or economical with resources

3. Kleptomaniac (चोरी करने की मानसिक बीमारी वाला व्यक्ति): A person with an uncontrollable urge to steal

4. Philanthropist (परोपकारी, दानवीर): A person who helps others, especially through charitable donations

5. Ubiquitous (सर्वव्यापी): Present or found everywhere

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Extremely idealistic and unrealistic, often in an impractical way.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Quixotic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Quixotic" means unrealistic and idealistic, from the character Don Quixote in Cervantes' novel, known for impractical, idealistic pursuits. (अव्यावहारिक)
◦ Example: His quixotic plan to eliminate poverty in a year impressed no economist.

 

• Quixotic is the opposite of Pragmatic — one chases idealistic dreams, the other deals with practical reality.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Pragmatic (व्यावहारिक): Dealing with things sensibly and realistically.

 

• Option 2: Cynical (निंदावादी, संशयी): Believing that people are motivated only by self-interest.

 

• Option 4: Skeptical (संशयवादी): Not easily convinced; having doubts.

 

NOTE

 

• Words derived from literary or fictional figures: Quixotic (Don Quixote, impractical idealism), Machiavellian (Machiavelli, cunning and scheming), Herculean (Hercules, requiring great strength), Utopian (Thomas More's Utopia, idealistic).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Altruist (परोपकारी, परार्थी): A person unselfishly concerned for others' welfare

2. Fastidious (चूज़ी, नुक्ताचीनी करने वाला): Very attentive to detail; hard to please

3. Knack (विशेष कुशलता): A special skill or talent

4. Pessimist (निराशावादी): A person who expects the worst outcome

5. Usurper (सत्ता हड़पने वाला): A person who takes a position of power illegally

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The right to vote in public elections.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Franchise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Franchise" means the right to vote, from Old French franchir (to free), originally meaning a grant of freedom or special privilege. (मताधिकार)
◦ Example: Universal adult franchise was granted to all Indian citizens above 18 years of age.

 

• Franchise in the political sense means the right to vote; note it also has an unrelated business meaning, a license to trade under a company's name.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Citizenship (नागरिकता): The status of being a legal member of a state or country.

 

• Option 2: Amnesty (क्षमादान, सामान्य क्षमा): An official pardon for people convicted of offences.

 

• Option 4: Referendum (जनमत संग्रह): A general vote by the public on a single political question.

 

NOTE

 

• Civic-rights family: Suffrage (right to vote, a close synonym), Citizenship (legal membership of a state), Referendum (public vote on one issue), Plebiscite (direct vote of the people on an important issue).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ambivalent (दुविधाग्रस्त): Having mixed feelings about something

2. Fallacy (भ्रांति, तर्कदोष): A mistaken belief based on unsound argument

3. Kudos (प्रशंसा, श्रेय): Praise for an achievement

4. Prodigal (फ़िज़ूलख़र्ची करने वाला): Wastefully extravagant

5. Unanimous (सर्वसम्मत): Fully in agreement

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A signature, especially that of a famous person, written by their own hand.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Autograph.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Autograph" means signature of a famous person, from Greek autos (self) and graphein (to write). (हस्ताक्षर)
◦ Example: Fans lined up for hours to get the cricketer's autograph.

 

• The prefix "auto-" means self, so an Autograph is literally something written by one's own hand.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Manuscript (हस्तलिपि): A handwritten or typed document, especially before printed publication.

 

• Option 2: Facsimile (हूबहू प्रतिलिपि): An exact copy or reproduction of something, especially a document.

 

• Option 4: Epitaph (समाधि-लेख): An inscription on a tombstone in memory of the person buried there.

 

NOTE

 

• Writing and inscription family: Manuscript (handwritten document), Epitaph (tombstone inscription), Epigraph (inscription on a building or book), Calligraphy (art of beautiful handwriting).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Amnesia (स्मृतिलोप): Loss of memory

2. Facade (बनावटी रूप, बाहरी आवरण): A deceptive outward appearance

3. Kinship (रिश्तेदारी, नातेदारी): A sharing of characteristics or origins; family relationship

4. Panacea (सर्वरोगनाशक औषधि): A solution or remedy for all problems

5. Unscrupulous (बेईमान, अनैतिक): Having no moral principles

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Habitually telling lies; untruthful.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Mendacious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Mendacious" means habitually untruthful, lying, from Latin mendax (lying, false). (झूठा)
◦ Example: The mendacious witness was caught contradicting his own earlier statement.

 

• Mendacious (lying) is the opposite of Veracious (truthful) — both derive from Latin roots meaning falsehood and truth respectively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Credulous (भोला, जल्दी विश्वास कर लेने वाला): Too ready to believe things; easily deceived.

 

• Option 2: Tenacious (दृढ़, हठी): Holding firmly to something; persistent.

 

• Option 4: Loquacious (बातूनी): Very talkative.

 

NOTE

 

• Truth-related family: Veracious (truthful), Veracity (truthfulness, noun), Mendacity (untruthfulness, noun form of mendacious), Duplicitous (deceitful, double-dealing), Candid (honest and straightforward).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Bibliophile (पुस्तक-प्रेमी): A person who loves books

2. Gullible (भोला-भाला): Easily deceived or tricked

3. Laconic (अल्पभाषी): Using very few words

4. Quandary (दुविधा): A state of uncertainty over what to do

5. Vindictive (प्रतिशोधी): Having a strong desire for revenge
